# @vllnt/convex-push

> Convex component that sends push notifications from your backend straight to APNs, FCM and Web Push, with a device registry, retries and no relay service.

Install: `pnpm add @vllnt/convex-push@canary convex`. Use the `canary` tag until 0.1.0 is released: npm `latest` still points at an older first canary build. Requires `convex@^1.47.0` (component environment variables) and runs in the Convex default runtime. Keys (Apple `.p8`, Firebase service account, VAPID pair) are component env bound at mount, never function arguments. Version 0.1.0 is a canary: senders are tested against recorded provider responses, not real devices.

For coding agents: this file, `README.md`, `docs/API.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and the TypeScript `src/` ship in `node_modules/@vllnt/convex-push/` and match the installed version. Read them before writing code against this package.

## When to use

- Use it when your Convex backend sends push notifications to iOS (APNs), Android (FCM HTTP v1) or browsers (Web Push) with your own Apple key, Firebase service account or VAPID keys.
- Use it when you want the device registry, per-device delivery status, retries and dead-device cleanup inside your Convex deployment, with no third-party relay.
- Use it when another channel (for example a webhook) should share the same queue and retries: a custom provider is one host action.
- Do not use it when you want Expo's push service to hold your Apple and Google credentials and send for you: use `@convex-dev/expo-push-notifications`.
- Do not use it when you send to FCM topics or conditions instead of registered devices: use `firebase-admin` in a `"use node"` action.
